This will be her first season with the Tommies. \r\n\u003Cp>\u003Cb>THE MACDONALD FILE\u003C/b>\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cul>\r\n\t\u003Cli>Joins the Tommies after 12 seasons at St. Cloud State University in St. Cloud, Minnesota\u003C/li>\r\n\t\u003Cli>Compiled a 105-72-36 record with the Huskies and the 2023 NSIC Regular Season Championship\u003C/li>\r\n\t\u003Cli>3x NCAA Division II Tournament participant (2023-25)\u003C/li>\r\n\t\u003Cli>2x NSIC Coach of the Year (2023, 2025)\u003C/li>\r\n\t\u003Cli>Entering 2025, coached 42 All-NSIC and 10 All-Region honorees; coached 2023 NSIC Freshman of the Year Linsey Trapino\u003C/li>\r\n\t\u003Cli>Coached 131 NSIC All-Academic honorees\u003C/li>\r\n\t\u003Cli>Served as an assistant coach at Central Michigan University (2013-14) and Minnesota State (2008-13)\u003C/li>\r\n\t\u003Cli>Graduate assistant at South Dakota State (2007-08)\u003C/li>\r\n\t\u003Cli>Four-year member of Creighton University women's soccer team (2003-07)\u003C/li>\r\n\u003C/ul>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>\u003Cb>ST. PAUL, MINN. – \u003C/b>After a national search, the University of St. Thomas Vice President, Director of Athletics \u003Cdfn>\u003Ca href=\"https://tommiesports.com/staff-directory/dr-phil-esten/178\" rel=\"smarttag\" rev=\"178\">Dr. Phil Esten\u003C/a>\u003C/dfn> announced Gretta Macdonald will serve as the next head coach of the women's soccer program. Macdonald will be the fifth coach in program history.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>\"I am absolutely thrilled to welcome Gretta and her family to St. Paul and the University of St. Thomas,\" said Esten.  \"As we navigated through this process, Gretta's commitment to building culture was authentic and deliberate, which has proven to deliver comprehensive excellence on the pitch, in the classroom, and within the community.  She brings strong experience and a proven track record to our women's soccer program, while her commitment to the holistic student-athlete experience and competitive excellence aligns with the mission of both our athletics department and the University.  The future is bright with Gretta Macdonald leading our women's soccer program.\"\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>\"As a Minnesota native, I am grateful and excited for the opportunity to lead and transform the University of St. Thomas women's soccer program,\" commented Macdonald. \"I want to thank Director of Athletics Phil Overall, she compiled four 10-win seasons and eight NSIC Tournament appearances.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Prior to her move to St. Cloud State in 2014, Macdonald was an assistant soccer coach at Central Michigan University, where her responsibilities included Director of Internal Operations and Director of the CMU Soccer Academy. She also served as an assistant coach at Minnesota State from 2008-2013, taking on the role of interim head coach in 2013.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>A native of Pine Springs, Minnesota, Macdonald played collegiate soccer at Creighton University from 2003 to 2007, earning four letters, and was on the SAAC Committee and Team Leadership Council.
